11	## Persistence
12	
13	Default style for this whole session, every response, until user say "stop caveman" or "normal mode". Keep terse on long sessions no filler drift.
14	
15	Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra|wenyan-lite|wenyan-full|wenyan-ultra|off`.
16	
17	## Rules
18	
19	Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.
20	
21	Never drop not/never/no/only/except flip meaning worse than any token saved. Numbers, units exact.
22	
23	Never ADD word to sound caveman. Compression only style never grow output. No inserted pronoun or copula to fake broken grammar: "when it not" cost one token more than "when not" and say same thing. Keep correct verb form when correct form cost same "sees" one token, "see" one token, so mangle buy nothing and read worse. Same rule as abbreviations and arrows: if caveman phrasing not shorter than plain phrasing, use plain.
24	
25	Clarity register: mix ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English into caveman, always. One idea per sentence. Sentence short, target 20 words max. Active voice. Present tense where true. One word one meaning: same term for same thing every time, no synonym rotation. Instruction = imperative: "Run X", not "X should be run". Noun cluster 3 words max. Pronoun only with one clear referent, else repeat noun. Caveman cut filler; STE keep what make meaning unambiguous. Conflict between them → clarity win.
26	
27	Tool calls: fire direct. No preamble, plan, or progress note before or between calls. After result: next call direct or final answer never announce next call. Text before call only to clarify, warn security/irreversible, or resolve ambiguity.
28	
29	Follow explicit reply-language instructions from the user or project. Otherwise preserve the user's dominant language. Never switch because of example text or multilingual context elsewhere. text:
`bot.mjs` is written and works in my checks. It exports `deliver` and `recordDismissal`. It has no dependencies, so `package.json` is unchanged. I tested it with fake transport and consent stores and sent nothing real. I did not save any memory notes.

**What the checks showed**
- **Races:** 12 worker processes delivering the same briefing at once sent exactly one push and one in-app item, and all 12 returned `push: true, inApp: true`.
- **Outcomes:** each of these gave the expected `push`, `inApp`, `reason` and `resumeAt` values:
  - Too early for the user's timezone.
  - Past the morning window.
  - Snoozed.
  - Category off.
  - Category never asked.
  - Phone permission off.
  - Consent store down.
  - Push rejected.
  - Dismissal pause.
  - Same briefing retried.
  - Second briefing on the same day.
- **Retry after a rejected push:** a push the phone rejected can be retried later without a duplicate in-app item.

**How it behaves**
- **Timing:** a briefing push goes out between 07:00 and 11:00 in the user's timezone. Before 07:00 it waits until 07:00. After 11:00 it moves to the next morning, because the briefing would be stale. Other card types are blocked from 22:00 to 07:00.
- **Snooze:** a snoozed user gets nothing on either surface. `resumeAt` is the snooze end, moved forward to the next allowed push time if the snooze ends at night.
- **Category switched off:** nothing is sent. No `resumeAt` is given.
- **Category missing:** the in-app item is stored, but no push is sent.
- **Push withheld, in-app kept:**
  - Phone permission is `false`.
  - Consent has `push` or `notifications` set to `false`.
  - Consent has `marketing` set to `false` (non-briefing types only).
  - The consent store throws.
  - The timezone is invalid.
- **Duplicates:** the same candidate id is never pushed or stored in-app twice. Retries return the earlier result. Only one briefing push goes out per local day.
- **Dismissals:** `recordDismissal` counts swipes per user and type. After 3 swipes of one type within 7 days, pushes of that type pause and `resumeAt` is set.
- **State:** it lives in `STATE_DIR`, one file per user, written atomically with a lock file so several processes can share it. It survives a restart.

**Rules I chose because the spec didn't say**
- The consent purpose names (`push`, `notifications`, `marketing`) are my guess.
- The 07:00–11:00 window, the 3-dismissals-in-7-days rule and the one-briefing-per-day cap are my choices. All are constants at the top of the file.
- I treated a missing category as "never asked", so it gets no push.

If your app uses different consent names or windows, change those constants and the consent check.
